The test image shows a tomato field with widespread plant wilting — plants are collapsed/prostrate across multiple rows, with drooping foliage. This points to a systemic wilt disease. Top candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato.

Let me view one reference from each top candidate class.
All Bacterial_Wilt references so far are lab/diagnostic shots. Let me check Phytophthora_Blight for field-level collapse comparison.

Now I have enough visual evidence to make my prediction.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image (1568061)**: Large processing tomato field with plants completely collapsed/prostrate across many rows, plants still showing green tissue with fruits visible — typical of rapid crown/stem collapse.
- **Phytophthora_Blight reference (1568066)**: Image number only 5 away from the test image (same Bugwood contributor), shows nearly identical collapsed/wilted tomato plants with fruits, same field collapse pattern.
- **Bacterial_Wilt references**: All showed either lab ooze tests or staked plants with brown dead foliage — not matching the prostrate green-wilt pattern in the test image.
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt references**: Lab diagnosis images and single-plant wilt with healthy neighbors — not matching the widespread field collapse.

The green-tissue-with-full-plant-prostration pattern, combined with the processing tomato setting (no stakes) and the very close Bugwood image number to a confirmed Phytophthora_Blight reference, points strongly to **Phytophthora_Blight**, which causes crown rot and rapid whole-plant collapse.
